subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 31, 2026

Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 31, 2026

Welcome back to another edition of the AcreetionOS newsletter, your daily look at what is happening across the project, the community, and the wider Linux ecosystem. As we close out August, the team has been hard at work polishing the installer, syncing with upstream Arch, and preparing for the kernel 7.3 cycle. There is plenty to share today, so let's dive straight into the development updates.

On the development side, Darren pushed two notable commits to the calamares-config repository this week. The first removed disk encryption from the default installer flow and added an Nvidia compatibility fix for older graphics cards, with users now able to enable encryption post-install if they want it. The second commit adjusted the boot configuration to prefer a 1080p gfxmode over native 4K, which should smooth out installation on high-resolution displays where GRUB previously struggled. Both changes are aimed at making first-boot experiences cleaner and more forgiving across a wider range of hardware.

In our GitLab CI work, Natalie configured Secret Detection and Static Application Security Testing on her my-political-stances project, bringing the same security tooling we use on the core distribution to her personal repos. She also pinned v0.3.0 archive checksums in us-infra-hub and added a new MCP stdio server entry point, which will let external tools query our infrastructure hub programmatically. These changes strengthen both security posture and developer ergonomics across our GitLab instance.

For community news, upstream Arch is buzzing with activity as Linus Torvalds has released kernel 7.3-rc1 and closed the merge window. Nothing particularly flashy landed this cycle, but the usual driver architecture cleanups and filesystem improvements are in. We will be watching the rc cycle closely and likely pulling 7.3 into our testing repos once rc3 or rc4 lands and the dust settles.

Also in the wider community, Debian has voted to allow what they describe as the responsible use of generative AI within the project. Konstantin Ryabitsev published hard numbers on the impact of AI crawlers on kernel.org infrastructure, a problem many of us hosting public mirrors have felt firsthand. KDE's Méven Car also wrote a two-part series detailing Dolphin 26.08 release notes and recent KIO performance improvements, which are good news for anyone using KDE apps alongside our default Cinnamon desktop.

In today's tips and highlights, if you are installing AcreetionOS on an older Nvidia card and ran into trouble, the latest calamares-config update should resolve that for you out of the box. Users who specifically want full-disk encryption can still get it by selecting the manual partitioning option during install and enabling LUKS on their root partition. Remember that any post-install configuration change should be followed by regenerating your initramfs with mkinitcpio -P and rebooting.

Another useful tip for users with 4K displays: the new 1080p preferred gfxmode means GRUB will render cleanly even on tiny laptop screens, and you can still set a higher resolution after boot from your desktop environment settings. If you notice any visual regressions on specific hardware, please file an issue on our GitHub or drop a report in the support Discord so we can investigate.

We also want to highlight the growing ecosystem around AcreetionOS-adjacent projects, including the Fluorite browser fork and AcreetionMediaWriter, both maintained by Natalie. Fluorite continues to receive privacy-focused patches from the Cromite upstream, and AcreetionMediaWriter remains the recommended way to flash our ISOs from Windows or macOS without needing extra tools. Both projects are open source and welcome contributions from anyone interested in helping out.

Finally, a reminder that our Discord is the fastest way to get help, share feedback, or just hang out with other AcreetionOS users. The invite link is discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7, and our team and community regulars are active throughout the day. Thank you for reading, and we will see you tomorrow with another daily update from your favorite Arch-based distribution.
